name: Heparin (unfractionated)
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Full-dose therapy, continuous IV infusion (68 kg adult)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 5,000 units IV bolus, then 20,000 to 40,000 units per 24 hours, adjusted to coagulation tests
5,000 units IV, then 10,000 to 20,000 units SC; then 8,000 to 10,000 units every 8 hours or 15,000 to 20,000 units every 12 hours
5,000 units SC 2 hours before surgery, then every 8 to 12 hours for 7 days or until ambulatory

key_interactions.action: Draw PT at least 5 hours after IV or 24 hours after SC heparin.

serious: Major or fatal bleeding (including adrenal and retroperitoneal)
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia with thrombosis (can occur weeks after stopping)
Fatal medication errors from vial confusion

contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to heparin or pork products
Inability to monitor coagulation for full-dose heparin (where required)
Uncontrolled active bleeding (except from disseminated intravascular coagulation)

pk.metabolism: Saturable cellular uptake (endothelium, macrophages) plus slower first-order clearance

sources.citation: Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC. (2026). Heparin sodium injection [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA017029, set ID 2a173253-dfdc-4d9d-8dee-b9c13e6fa9f5, version effective April 30, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.
